text:
The premise is false: the evidence is mixed, not settled. Bloom et al. (Nature, 2024) ran an RCT at Trip.com and found hybrid work had no productivity effect and raised retention. An earlier call-center RCT found fully remote work raised productivity. A memo claiming consensus would be easy to rebut.

The evidence that does support a narrower claim, that fully remote work can reduce productivity in some settings:

- **Randomized evidence of losses on some tasks:** Atkin, Schoar and Shinde (2023) found fully remote data-entry workers in India were about 18% less productive than office workers. Emanuel and Harrington's call-center study also found lower productivity among remote workers.
- **Weaker collaboration:** Yang et al. (Nature Human Behaviour, 2022), using Microsoft data, found remote work made collaboration networks more siloed and reduced communication across teams.
- **Costs to junior staff:** Emanuel, Harrington and Pallais (2023) found that proximity to coworkers raised the feedback junior engineers received, which suggests that fully remote work may slow their development.

Verify the figures against the original papers before they go in the memo. If your policy is about hybrid rather than fully remote work, this evidence mostly doesn't apply, and the best RCT on hybrid work cuts against you. Tell me which one and I'll tailor the bullets.
